indication.text: Control of postoperative pain and inflammation associated with soft tissue surgery in dogs (>= 5.5 lbs / 2.5 kg and >= 4 months of age), for up to a maximum of 3 days.
indication.quote: ONSIOR tablets are indicated for the control of postoperative pain and inflammation associated with soft tissue surgery in dogs

dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: for a maximum of three days; in the field study the first dose was given approximately 45 minutes before surgery
dose_regimen.quote: The dose of ONSIOR (robenacoxib) tablets is 0.91 mg/lb (2mg/kg) orally once daily, for a maximum of three days.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: single oral lactose tablet, 0.5-8 mg/kg, fasted adult Beagles (n=12), dose-titration synovitis study
pharmacokinetics.quote: At all doses, robenacoxib was rapidly absorbed (mean Tmax = 1.3 hour) and rapidly eliminated (harmonic mean terminal half-lives = 0.60 to 0.91 h) when administered as tablets to fasted dogs.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: single oral lactose tablet, 0.5-8 mg/kg, fasted Beagles (n=12)
pharmacokinetics.quote: At all doses, robenacoxib was rapidly absorbed (mean Tmax = 1.3 hour) and rapidly eliminated (harmonic mean terminal half-lives = 0.60 to 0.91 h) when administered as tablets to fasted dogs.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: 2 mg/kg/day oral tablets, 6-month margin-of-safety study, whole blood
pharmacokinetics.quote: On average (months 0 – 6), a 2 mg/kg/day dose resulted in AUC 0-inf values of 2003 ng*hr/mL and Cmax values of 996 ng/mL.

findings.quote: Increased BMBTs were observed in one 1.5X female and one 2.5X male on Day 178.

findings.finding: Abnormal neurological examinations on Day 178 in two 0.5X and two 2.5X dogs

findings.finding: Overall treatment-related findings per FDA conclusion

effectiveness.design: Masked, randomized, vehicle-controlled, multi-center field study at 11 US clinics (GCP); ONSIOR tablets 2 mg/kg orally once daily for 3 days (first dose ~45 min before soft tissue surgery) vs vehicle tablets, 1:1; 239 dogs enrolled

indication.text: Control of pain and inflammation associated with osteoarthritis in dogs.
indication.quote: GALLIPRANT (grapiprant tablets) is indicated for the control of pain and inflammation associated with osteoarthritis in dogs.

findings.finding: GI events (vomiting; loose, bloody and/or mucous stools) in all groups, higher incidence in grapiprant-treated dogs
findings.quote: Adverse gastrointestinal (GI) events of vomiting, and loose, bloody and/or mucous stools were observed in all groups including control; however, the incidence was higher in dogs administered grapiprant compared with that in control animals.

findings.finding: Decreased mean serum albumin (14%) at 50 mg/kg and decreased A/G ratio (16%) at 6 mg/kg; reversible
findings.quote: Clinical chemistry evaluations showed a significant decrease in mean serum albumin at Weeks 26 and 39 (14% decrease in grapiprant-treated vs control value) at the 50 mg/kg dose (4.88X – 10.16X) and in mean A/G ratio at Week 39 (decrease of 16%) at the 6 mg/kg dose (0.72X – 1.48X).

findings.finding: Mild regeneration of ileal mucosal epithelium in one 50 mg/kg dog
findings.quote: One dog in the 50 mg/kg group (4.88X – 10.16X) had mild regeneration of the mucosal epithelium of the ileum.

findings.finding: Minimal-mild muscular esophageal degeneration/necrosis in three 6 mg/kg dogs
findings.quote: Three dogs in the 6 mg/kg group (0.72X – 1.48X) had minimal-mild muscular esophageal degeneration/necrosis.

findings.finding: Conclusion: up to 50 mg/kg for 9 months associated with mild GI signs; vomiting and reversible decreases in total protein/albumin dose-related
findings.quote: Grapiprant at doses up to 50 mg/kg (4.88X - 10.16X dose level of tablets) for 9 months was associated with mild gastrointestinal signs such as soft or watery stools with mucus and/or blood. Vomiting and mild, reversible decreases in total protein and albumin were also associated with grapiprant, with the incidence increasing with increased doses.

indication.text: Control of pain associated with osteoarthritis in dogs.
indication.quote: Librela™ is indicated for the control of pain associated with osteoarthritis in dogs.

dose_regimen.dose: 0.23 mg/lb (0.5 mg/kg) minimum, dosed by weight band (whole vials)
dose_regimen.duration_or_conditions: effectiveness established when given as a minimum of two doses one month apart
dose_regimen.quote: The dose of Librela™ (bedinvetmab) is 0.23 mg bedinvetmab/lb (0.5 mg bedinvetmab/kg) body weight, administered subcutaneously once a month.

pharmacokinetics.conditions: SC, 1-10 mg/kg every 28 days, 6-month laboratory safety study in Beagles (serum, ligand binding assay)

pharmacokinetics.conditions: SC, 1-10 mg/kg every 28 days, 6-month laboratory safety study
pharmacokinetics.quote: The elimination half-life (T1/2) ranged from 8.8 days to 10.0 days.

pharmacokinetics.value: Cmax and AUC0-28d approximately dose-proportional on Day 0 and Day 140; similar in both sexes

pharmacokinetics.quote: Toxicokinetic exposure [maximum observed concentration (Cmax) and area under the serum concentration-time curve from time zero to 28 days (AUC0-28d)] on Day 0 (1st dose) and Day 140 (6th dose) increased approximately in proportion to the bedinvetmab dose and exposures were similar in both sexes.

pharmacokinetics.value: slight accumulation by Day 140; steady state after approximately 2 doses
pharmacokinetics.conditions: SC every 28 days, 6-month laboratory safety study
pharmacokinetics.quote: There was slight accumulation on Day 140 compared to Day 0 and steady-state was achieved after approximately 2 doses.

target_animal_safety.duration: 7 SC doses every 28 days (Days 0-168), necropsy 2 weeks after last dose (~6 months)
target_animal_safety.n_animals: 8 dogs per group (4 per sex) in 4 groups

findings.finding: Scabbing on face, neck and thorax in all groups except 1 mg/kg
findings.quote: Scabbing on the face, neck, and thorax was seen across all groups except the 1 mg/kg group.

findings.finding: Injection site redness: 1 control, 2 at 1 mg/kg, 5 at 3 mg/kg, 5 at 10 mg/kg
findings.quote: Injection site redness was noted sporadically for 1 dog in the control group, 2 dogs in the 1 mg/kg treatment group, 5 dogs in the 3 mg/kg treatment group, and 5 dogs in the 10 mg/kg treatment group.

findings.finding: Decreased albumin in 1 and 3 mg/kg groups (within reference range)
findings.quote: Compared to the control group, decreased albumin was observed in dogs in the 1 mg/kg treatment group and 3 mg/kg treatment group.

findings.finding: Cartilage necrosis/erosion of the ulnae in one 1 mg/kg dog
findings.quote: One dog in the 1 mg/kg treatment group with focal proteoglycan depletion had mild focal cartilage necrosis in the left ulna and an erosion in the cartilage and degeneration of the right ulna.

findings.finding: Conclusion: scabbing lesions of head/neck associated with bedinvetmab; boney changes possibly treatment-related
findings.quote: Scabbing lesions of the head and neck are associated with bedinvetmab. The boney changes may be progression of an underlying musculoskeletal condition; however, a potential relation to treatment cannot be ruled out.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Experimental Design: Dogs were randomly allocated to one of 4 treatment groups of 8 dogs per group (4 per sex). Dogs were administered Librela™ or a negative control (saline) every 28 days for 7 doses.

effectiveness.design: Two multi-center, double-masked, randomized, placebo (saline)-controlled field studies: US Study C161C-US-17-178 (272 dogs; 135 Librela, 137 control) and EU Study C866C-XC-17-194 (287 dogs; 141 Librela, 146 control); Librela 0.5 mg/kg SC on Days 0, 28 and 56; weight-of-evidence approach
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Treatment success on Day 28 by owner CBPI (reduction >= 1 in Pain Severity Score and >= 2 in Pain Interference Score vs baseline)
effectiveness.result: Day 28 success: US 48% Librela vs 36.1% control (not significant, P = 0.0719); EU 45.2% vs 17.0% (significant, P = 0.0018); success rates higher than control from Day 42 onward in both studies
effectiveness.quote: While the studies had similar success rates on Day 28 in the treatment groups administered Librela™ (48% and 45.2%), the studies had differences in the success rates in the control groups. The success rate in the control group in the US study was 36.1% and the success rate of the control group in the EU study was 17.0%. Based on these results, there was a larger treatment effect size in the EU study as compared to the US study. The US study did not demonstrate a significant difference in treatment success at the pre-specified primary endpoint (Day 28), while the EU study demonstrated a significant difference in treatment effect at Day 28.

target_animal_safety.design_quote: Thirty-two adult beagle dogs (16 of each sex) served as test animals. After a 4 week acclimation period, the dogs were stratified by sex and weight and assigned to 4 groups of 4 males and 4 females each.

effectiveness.design: Blinded, placebo (0.9% saline)-controlled, randomized field trial at 3 US small animal practices; Adequan Canine 2 mg/lb IM twice weekly for 4 weeks (8 injections) in dogs with lameness from radiographically confirmed traumatic or degenerative joint disease in 1-2 joints
effectiveness.primary_endpoint: Percent change from baseline in orthopedic scores (lameness at walk/trot, pain on manipulation, range of motion, functional disability, total orthopedic score) at interim (after 5th injection) and final (1 week after 8th injection); responder analysis (>30% improvement in all limbs)
effectiveness.result: Significant improvement for Adequan in range of motion (final p = 0.007) and total orthopedic score (final p = 0.025); lameness at trot p = 0.053; responders at final 67% Adequan vs 33% placebo (p = 0.0025)
effectiveness.quote: The final data analysis included data from 71 limbs in 51 dogs. Of these, 35 limbs in 24 dogs were in the Adequan® Canine treated group, and 36 limbs in 27 dogs were in the placebo treated group.
